name: relay
description: One panel for every AI coding session: Claude, Codex and friends, with forks.

enumDescriptions: Run sessions through the installed Claude Code and Codex CLIs.
Fake providers with seeded sessions, for working on the UI.

relay.claudePath.description: Path to the claude executable. Empty: look on PATH and the usual install locations.

relay.codexPath.description: Path to the codex executable. Empty: look on PATH and the usual install locations.

relay.chromePath.description: Path to the Chrome (or other Chromium browser) executable used by Open in Browser. Empty: look in the usual install locations.

relay.tailscalePath.description: Path to the tailscale executable used by Remote Access. Empty: look on PATH and in the Tailscale app.

relay.titleModel.description: Codex model that writes each session's title from your latest message. Without Codex, the title is the message's first line.

relay.keepAwake.description: Keep the computer from idle-sleeping while an agent is working (macOS). The display can still sleep.

relay.modelHints.markdownDescription: Suggest a model for each message: [Jev](https://typesafe.ai) rates how hard the message looks, and the suggestion shows next to the model dropdown. After a session's first message only the effort changes, so the prompt cache is kept. **⇧⌘↵** sends with it. Messages you type are sent to TypeSafe. Asks for your TypeSafe API key the first time; **Relay: Set Jev API Key** changes it.

relay.modelHintModels.markdownDescription: The model and effort suggested for a `simple`, `standard` or `complex` message, per provider. Models are the ids in the model dropdown (hover a model to see it). A model the provider doesn't list gets no suggestion. Easiest to change in Relay's settings (the gear in the sessions bar).

relay.newSessionModel.markdownDescription: Provider, model and effort a new session starts with, e.g. `{ "provider": "claude", "model": "opus", "effort": "high" }`. Empty: the first provider's first model. Models are the ids in the model dropdown.

relay.newSessionWorktree.description: New sessions start with their own git worktree, merged back on Complete. The toggle in a new session's header still switches it for that session.

relay.newSessionBrowser.description: New sessions start with access to Relay's browser. The toggle in a new session's header still switches it for that session.

relay.planPrompt.default:
Before writing any code, let's plan. Read whatever you need to understand the request, but don't edit files or run anything that changes state.

Then briefly say how you'd approach it, and ask me the questions you need answered to do it well: anything unclear, missing, or with more than one reasonable way to go. Number them. For each, list the options you see and say which you'd pick and why. Only ask what actually changes the result; decide the rest from the code and sensible defaults.

Stop there and wait for my answers.
relay.planPrompt.markdownDescription: Added to the end of a message sent in **Plan** mode (the dropdown next to effort). The chat shows only what you typed.

relay.askPrompt.default: Just answer. Don't change anything: no editing files and no commands that change state. Read files and search the code as much as you need to give an accurate answer.
relay.askPrompt.markdownDescription: Added to the end of a message sent in **Ask** mode (the dropdown next to effort). The turn also runs read-only: the agent can read and search files but not edit them or run commands that change things.

relay.outputFormat.markdownDescription: Add `#relay.outputFormatPrompt#` to the end of every message, so you control how the agent formats its answers.

relay.outputFormatPrompt.default: Keep answers short and easy to read. For a simple question, answer in one line. For a complex one, give the most compact answer first, then expand only if really needed.
relay.outputFormatPrompt.markdownDescription: Added to the end of every message when `#relay.outputFormat#` is on, after the **Plan** or **Ask** instruction, and introduced by a fixed line that tells the agent it's a style for the reply, not part of the task. The chat shows only what you typed.

enumDescriptions: VS Code notification, plus a macOS notification with a sound when VS Code isn't the focused app.
No notifications; the activity bar badge still counts sessions to review.
relay.notifications.description: How to get your attention when a session you aren't looking at finishes, fails or needs approval.
